source.question: F-12's water cut fell from about 0.97 to about 0.3 at the end of 2014. What was done to the well, and why did the plug set in 2010 not do the same?

submission.summary: F-12’s water cut fell from about 0.97 to 0.31 after a workover on 2014-11-26 that set a plug at 3 150 m to isolate the lower water zones and perforated a new oil zone from 3 126 to 3 140 m, lifting oil from 177 to 857 Sm3/d. The 2010 plug at 3 210 m was set deep in the lower blank pipe, cutting only about 33% of the water with no new perforations, so water cut was unchanged.

findings.claim: On 2014-11-26 the well was worked over to install a 7" plug at 3 150 m and perforate a new zone from 3 126 to 3 140 m.
findings.detail: well_operations F-12 2014-11-26: Installed 7" EV0 plug with mid element at 3150 m. Perforated new zone from 3126,2 -3139,7 mMD. Prior perforations 3131-3147, 3161-3180, 3220-3257; blank pipes 3147-3161, 3180-3220.

findings.claim: Water cut fell from 0.965 to 0.338 after the job while oil rose to 857 Sm3/d.
findings.detail: production_log plugs_set 2014-11-26 depth 3150: 60-day window 2014-09-23 to 2014-11-22 water_cut 0.965 oil 177 Sm3/d; 28-day window 2014-11-29 to 2015-01-28 water_cut 0.338 oil 857 Sm3/d. Monthly 2014-11 0.9623 and 2015-01 0.3107; daily 2014-10 around 0.97 and 2015-01-02 0.2242 with 60 days before and 28 days after.

findings.claim: The 2010 plug at 3 210 m added no new perforations and water cut moved from 0.638 to 0.676.
findings.detail: well_operations 2010-09-23: Installed 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 3210 m mid element, no perforations. production_log plugs_set 2010-09-23 depth 3210: 60-day window 2010-07-22 to 2010-09-20 water_cut 0.638 oil 1850 Sm3/d; 59-day window 2010-09-24 to 2010-11-23 water_cut 0.676 oil 1612 Sm3/d. Therefore the plug did not lower water cut.

findings.claim: The 2010 PLT shows water entered mainly above 3 210 m, so that plug could cut only about 33% of the water.
findings.detail: PLT 2010-09 low rate oil 3132 to 3165 half below 3162, water 3165 to 3243 half below 3169; at blank pipe 3180-3220 below_top water_share 0.333 low rate and 0.379 medium rate, oil_share 0.01 and 0.015, water_cut_left_above 0.511 and 0.516. At blank pipe 3147-3161 below_top water_share 0.981 low and 1.0 medium. Plug at 3210 in 3180-3220 gap cuts little water; the main water was higher.

findings.claim: The 2014 plug at 3 150 m in the upper gap cut about 98% of the water on the log, but the new perforations replaced the oil.
findings.detail: At blank pipe 3147-3161 below_top oil_share 0.814 low / 0.752 medium, water_share 0.981 / 1.0, of_flow_left 0.812 / 0.748 oil, 0.972 / 1.0 water, oil_kept_above 0.188 / 0.252. Plug at 3150 isolates all below including 3161-3180 oil; without new zone 3126.2-3139.7 the well would lose 75% to 81% of oil. Therefore 2014 job kept oil while cutting water, 2010 job had no makeup.

Dismounted and mounted tension cylinders. RIH with production riser to 100 m MD.

Retrieved landing string. Installed BPV. Nippled down BOP and Riser. Installed dart in BPV. Terminated control lines. Installed extension spool.
Installed the WH extension spool, Xmas tree and the production Co-flex hose.
Leak tested X-mas tree connections to 30/345 bars 5/10 min. Lined up and leak tested production line 50/180 bars 5/10 min. Inflow tested LMV and HMV against BPV.
Sent firing command to E-Fire firing head in TCP guns and perforated well from 3130 to 3281 mMDRT.

Handed well over from Production. RU HMV and DHSV to local control panel. Installed test and bleed manifold on to XMT KWV. Performed line test from KWV to cmt unit. Attempted to leak tested XMT cross to 30/200 bar for 5/10 min.

Operated and greased up leaking PWV. Leak tested XMT cross to 30/200 bar for 5/10 min. Installed WL BOP and riser on XMT. Tested shear seals on WL BOP. Installed combination toolstring in riser. POOH and prepared for inflow test of HMV.

Inflow tested HMV to 81-5 bar/10 min. Broke lubricator and LD toolstring. Installed PLT toolstring in riser. MU lubricator and leak tested at in-situ sub. Equalized and opened HMV. RIH with PLT toolstring on 7/16" EWL from surface to 2929 m. Performed stationary logging at DHPG depth. Continued RIH from 2929 m to 3030 m to perform shut-in station logs and 4 PLT tool calibration passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Bean up well to 4500 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 high rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Choked back flow to 3000 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 medium rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD.

Choked back flow to 1500 Sm3/day. Performed station logs and 4 low rate flowing PLT passes in the interval 3030 m to 3255 m MD. Shut-in well. POOH with PLT toolstring. Inflow tested DHSV, HMV and MMV for handover. BO lubricator and LD toolstring. LD lubricator. RD and LD WL riser.

RD BOP from XMT. Leak test XMT cross, KWV and tree cap. Hand well over to Mærsk Production. Cleared and cleaned rig floor of remaining WL equipment. Transferred operation to F-99 for PRS-and 5-yearly BOP classification.
Waited on access to well. Took over well. Rigged up WL riser and BOP.

RU WL equipment. Installed BHA into lubricator. RIH with PLT. Performed spinner calibration. Performed depth correlation with GR/CCL. Took stationary reading at 2929 m. Ran PLT shut in pass. Took stationary readings. Beaned up well. Waited for stable flow.

Waited for stable flow aprox. 5050 Sm3/d with PLT at 3080 m. Attempted to RIH at various speed. No-go. Reduced flow rate to 3000 Sm3/d. Took stationary readings at 3080, 3155, 3200 and 3250 m. Logged flowing passes between 3030 and 3250 m, down at 40 m/min and up at 10/20/30/40 m/min. Reduced flow rate to 1500 Sm3/d. Logged flowing passes between 3000 and 3250 m, down at 40 m/min and up at 10/20/30/40 m/min. Unable to log down on both flowing rates at 10/20/30 m/min. POOH with PLT. Changed tool string. RIH with 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 800 m.
Installed 5,72" EVO bridge plug at 3210 m mid element. RD wireline pressure control equipment and handed well over to production department.
Spotted some equpment. Waited on weather, wind above 40 knots.
Spotted WL equipment. Checked equipment together with rig electrician.
Spotted equipment. Well handed over from Production dept. to D&W. Started to rig up on wellhead.

Completed rigging up wireline equipment. Leak tested rig up to 20/345 bar. Run in hole with Halliburton EVO plug. Pulled out of hole after tool failure at 1400 m. Started to prepare back up toolstring.
Installed 7" EV0 plug with mid element at 3150 m. Perforated new zone from 3126,2 -3139,7 mMD. POOH with perforating gun.
POOH with perfoartion gun. Inflow tested well barriers. Rigged down WL equipment. Operation completed.

result.note: Daily reports exist for drilling and for work on the well (wireline, plugs, perforations, production logs), not for days of normal production. A job's date is the day the work was done; kind is drilling, completion, workover (work on a producing or injecting well) or abandonment. Ask for one day to see every operation line.

surveys.read_from: plots in Volve 15/9-F-12 Production Logging Interpretation Results, March 2009 (pages 14, 15, 16), pictures with no data behind them, read by sam-3.1 from the prompt 'green area'

report_says.quote: ~83% of oil produced from the upper 2 completions, the rest from the lower 3

surveys.read_from: LAS files of the interpreted log (Well_logs_pr_WELL/15_9-F-12/10.PRODUCTION LOGS/PLT Sept 2010)

result.note: A production log measures the flow passing each depth while the well flows; going up, it grows past each zone that produces. A share at a depth is the part of the pass's oil or water entering below that depth (1 at the bottom of the well's inflow, 0 above the top zone). comes_in_from_m to to_m holds 90% of each phase's inflow. Only shares are given: the files' rates have no units, and the plots' are downhole volumes. A plug set at a depth shuts off what enters below it: the shares below say what it could remove, not what it did, and never what it keeps (an oil_share of 0.7 is 70% of the oil cut off and 30% left; oil_kept_above is what stays); plugs_set gives what each plug already set did to the well (water cut and oil before and after). A bridge plug is set in blank pipe, never inside a perforated interval (inside_perforation_m names the interval a depth falls in; blank_pipe_m lists the gaps, and each pass's at_blank_pipe gives the shares below the top and the bottom of every gap: the depths a plug can actually be set at). A plug set after a survey (its plugs_set_since) already shut off what entered below it: on that log a depth or gap at or below it is already_isolated (a plug there cuts nothing new), and of_flow_left gives what a shallower plug would cut as a share of the flow left above the old plug. water_cut_left_above is the water cut of the flow entering above a depth on that pass, what a plug there would leave flowing (for a gap, a plug anywhere in it): compare it with the well's water cut now to say what a plug would change. rate_vs_well is the pass's surface rate over the well's own in the month before: a pass run far below it may weight the zones differently. since_survey says how old the latest log is and how far the water cut has moved since: an old log may no longer show where the water enters, and a new one would settle it. Each survey's passes were run at several surface rates. A survey read off pictures carries the checks of that reading.

result.no_trend: WOR is not rising with cumulative oil on 2013-05 to 2016-08: no limit can be projected
result.notes: WOR = water/oil by month; the trend is log10(WOR) against cumulative oil, fitted on up to 36 recent months with WOR >= 1. The water cuts in to_limits are reference points, not an economic limit: the data holds no costs or prices, so remaining_oil_sm3 says how much oil is left before each, not whether it pays. field_voidage: replacement_ratio is injection over voidage at reservoir conditions (Bo 1.385 m3/Sm3 from PUD p.20, low/high with Bo 1.5/1.27; Bw 1; above the bubble point, so no free gas); surface_ratio is the same in surface volumes, which overstates replacement.
